title: Wihtgar
capsule: The Wihtwara (Old English: Ƿihtƿara, 'people of the Isle of Wight') were a Jutish people who settled the Isle of Wight during the fifth- and sixth-century Anglo-Saxon migrations. According to Bede and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, Stuf and Wihtgar—nephews of the West Saxon founder Cerdic—received the island from Cynric around 534, though Wihtgar himself may be a legendary figure invented to explain the island's name. The kingdom survived as a distinct political entity until 686, when the West Saxon king Cædwalla invaded, slew the last king Arwald in battle, and had Arwald's baptised brothers immediately executed, completing the Wessex annexation and Christianisation of the island.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent—the Isle of Wight itself—is clear, but all early rulers and dates rest on Bede and the Chronicle, which are retrospective and contain legendary elements; the early sixth-century dates are particularly uncertain.
